ethanol inhibits pinocytosis in the rat yolk sac.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of maternal ethanol administration on the development and function of the fetal yolk sac, which is the first organ of the mammalian conceptus to come into contact with the maternal circulation.
the effects of ethanol on the yolk sac and placenta in the pregnant rat.
the effects of ethanol on placental function in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ethanol inhibits yolk sac function and that the mechanism of action of this inhibition may be of importance to the mechanism of action as a teratogenic agent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethanol inhibits pinocytosis in yolk sacs in vitro, and that this inhibition is reversible.
ethanol inhibits yolk sac pinocytosis, proteolysis and histiotrophic nutrition.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the yolk sac may be a target organ for the effects of alcohol during pregnancy.

the acute administration to a pregnant rat of ethanol in concentrations of 0.01 and/or 0.05% (v/v) may give rise to maternal blood and uterine concentrations of ethanol that inhibit pinocytosis in the visceral yolk sac and that this inhibition may persist for several hours.
ethanol is a potent inhibitor of pinocytotic uptake and proteolytic activity of the visceral yolk sac in the rat, an effect that is reversible but may have teratogenic consequences.
